newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran top judge rejects U.S. human rights criticism.
newsitem.headline: Iran top judge rejects U.S. human rights criticism.

text.p: Iran's senior judge on Monday rejected U.S. criticism of the Islamic republic's human rights record, saying Washington had a habit of accusing those countries it did not control of rights abuses.

"America's government disregards international practices and accuses every country that is not under its hegemony of being a violator of human rights," head of judiciary Ayatollah Mohammad Yazdi was quoted by Tehran radio as saying.
Yazdi's remarks came a few days after a U.S. State Department annual report said there was no significant improvement in Iran's human rights record.
"America's government sees the prosecution of people who disrupt public order, bandits and drug smugglers as human rights violations," Yazdi said, without referring directly to the report.
The report, which was released on Thursday, accused Iran of abuses including extrajudicial killings, summary executions, diappearances and widespread torture.
